summary: Backend-only iteration_5 verification of the LOCKED_SUPPLIER_CAP=60 + Semaphore=60 architecture for the user-reported bug (q='Kit,chaine,distribution', 616 candidates → count=0). The cap architecture is CORRECTLY IMPLEMENTED and the FadPro variant fallback DID resolve OEM 1608745980 to 8 items in supplier_lookup_cache (matched_variant='1608745980'). HOWEVER the user-reported bug is NOT FIXED end-to-end: GET /api/oem-stock-search still returns count=0 / items=[] because the 45 s global asyncio.wait_for() trips before lookup() finishes — observed at 45.16 s (cold) AND 45.15 s (warm rerun). Backend log confirms 'oem-stock-search global timeout for q=Kit,chaine,distribution'. ROOT CAUSE: piecesautos.tn vehicle-compat scraping (get_compat_list, server.py L1247) is the bottleneck, NOT supplier lookups — dozens of 'piecesautos search failed: ReadTimeout' warnings during the run with pa_sem=10 means 100+ compat fetches × 5-10 s each easily exceed 45 s, cancelling gather() and dropping ALL items.

critical.issue: Global timeout still fires at 45 s on BOTH cold and warm cache (45.16s cold / 45.15s warm) → count=0 items=[] despite FadPro cache having 530 rows incl. ref=1608745980 with 8 items. Root cause: piecesautos.tn compatibility scraping via get_compat_list() — log shows many 'piecesautos search failed: ReadTimeout' during the run with pa_sem=10 parallelism. User-reported bug NOT resolved end-to-end.

minor.issue: Copia/PartsPro cache rows = 61 each instead of strict <= 60 — a race in semaphore queueing allowed one extra call past LOCKED_SUPPLIER_CAP. Minor — doesn't affect correctness.
No per-call timeout — relies on httpx default. ReadTimeouts cost several seconds each and compound under pa_sem=10.

action_items: CRITICAL: The cap architecture (Semaphore=60, LOCKED_SUPPLIER_CAP=60) is correctly implemented but does NOT fix the user-reported bug because the bottleneck is get_compat_list() (piecesautos.tn scraping), not the supplier lookups. Options for main agent E1: (a) GATE the vehicle-compatibility filter behind a separate cap (PA_COMPAT_CAP) the same way Copia/PartsPro are capped — only call piecesautos.tn for the first N picked items; (b) add explicit per-call timeout to pa_fetch (e.g. asyncio.wait_for(pa_fetch(ref), timeout=2.0)) so ReadTimeouts don't accumulate; (c) bump the global timeout from 45 s → 90 s (still under Cloudflare 100 s) which alone would let the warm path finish in ~50-60 s; (d) BEST: when the global asyncio.wait_for fires, surface PARTIAL results from any already-completed lookup() coroutines instead of returning empty all_results=[]. Recommended combination: (a) + (b) + (d).
Tighten Copia/PartsPro queue admission so the count never exceeds 60 — currently 61 each.
Add a per-call timeout to pa_fetch in /app/backend/server.py to prevent piecesautos.tn ReadTimeouts (5–10 s each) from compounding under pa_sem=10.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L1154 sem=asyncio.Semaphore(60) and L1155 LOCKED_SUPPLIER_CAP=60 are correctly declared at module-level inside the endpoint.
server.py L1269 lookup(c, idx): the idx<LOCKED_SUPPLIER_CAP gate is wired correctly and the enumerate at L1346 passes the index.

server.py L1247 get_compat_list(ref) is the unaddressed bottleneck — it's cached for 7 days but the cache is ref-keyed and cold for a fresh query like 'Kit,chaine,distribution' that touches new refs. With pa_sem=10 + per-fetch ReadTimeouts of 5–10 s, even 100+ refs needing compat checks alone exhaust the 45 s budget.

When asyncio.wait_for fires on the gather, all in-flight lookup() coroutines are cancelled and their picked items are lost. A try/except with asyncio.shield or a 'as_completed' pattern would preserve completed work.

server.py is now 1654 lines — the OEM-search endpoint alone is ~250 lines. Worth refactoring into a separate oem_search_service.py with: SupplierCapManager, PiecesautosCompatService, VariantFallbackResolver as separate classes. Not blocking this iteration.

rca_of_the_issue: USER-REPORTED BUG (q='Kit,chaine,distribution' → count=0): the iteration_5 architecture (Semaphore=60, LOCKED_SUPPLIER_CAP=60, FadPro unconditional, variant fallback to 6-digit prefix) is correctly implemented. The FadPro variant fallback DID surface 8 items for the user's reported OEM 1608745980 (visible in db.supplier_lookup_cache). HOWEVER the items never reach the HTTP response because the 45 s asyncio.wait_for global timeout (server.py L1347) fires before asyncio.gather completes — cancelling ALL lookup() coroutines and returning empty all_results=[]. The endpoint then returns count=0. The bottleneck is NOT supplier lookups (proven by warm-cache rerun at 45.15s identical to cold) but get_compat_list() at L1247, which scrapes piecesautos.tn live with pa_sem=10. Backend log shows dozens of 'piecesautos search failed: ReadTimeout' during the run. Each ReadTimeout costs 5–10 s; with 100+ picked items needing compat checks, total compat-time easily exceeds 45 s. FIX requires capping compat fetches (analogous to LOCKED_SUPPLIER_CAP) OR adding per-call timeouts to pa_fetch OR bumping the global timeout to 90 s OR surfacing partial results on timeout. Recommended: pa_fetch_cap=60 + per-call 2 s timeout + surface partial results.
